page: Microsoft Azure D32s_v3 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB L3 cache. The hardware configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. It is equipped with 262 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance trade-off between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core performance is consistently categorized as weak, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core, geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip and bzip3 operations. Conversely, multi-core performance scales to average levels across stress-ng multi-core, geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory scores, falls into the average category. In application-specific tests, the server maintains average performance for static web serving, Redis SET operations, and database operations. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference using small and medium models achieves average token generation speeds, whereas prompt processing for large models drops to poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32s_v3 offers a balanced resource density suitable for workloads that benefit from multi-threaded scaling rather than raw single-core speed. The inclusion of Premium Storage capability and 262 GB of local storage provides a solid foundation for database operations and general-purpose enterprise applications. However, the lack of hardware acceleration and poor large-model LLM inference performance make it unsuitable for advanced AI workloads. This server is best suited for multi-threaded application servers, static web serving, relational databases, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise workloads.
